output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error on our side, not to the fungicide, Lower Serra fruit or Meridane. When Meridane bookings moved to the new Tallis system, the mandarin product record was copied from avocados and carried a 7°C carriage temperature. Our specification is 4°C. All five Meridane containers were sent at 7°C and decayed 9–14%. The four Coastway containers and the one earlier Meridane booking (K1, booked by email) were at 4°C and were fine. Meridane's units held the setpoint we gave them, so a claim against them would fail. The new fungicide containers at 4°C passed, which clears the fungicide. Lower Serra pallets were somewhat worse, but they were only 28–40% of each container, so that is a secondary effect at most. Suspending them would punish the wrong party. Next steps, in order: correct the temperature in the Tallis mandarin record to 4°C. Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check that compares reefer settings against the product specification before each submission. Hold the claim, the suspension and the invoice deduction. Tell Nordhafen what happened. Confidence is high.
